summary: Clean. All seven focus areas (no hard-coded cookie flags, no log leakage, no CSRF regression, safe missing-attribute fallback, race-free singleton under WebFlux concurrency, backward-compat for pre-fix cookies, logout writes Max-Age=0) audited against OWASP A02 and A07 — pass. Cookie security flags (name, httpOnly, secure, sameSite, path, domain, partitioned) flow from ServerProperties via PropertyMapper.alwaysApplyingWhenNonNull (RememberMeWebSessionIdResolver.java:57-63), with safe seeded defaults (httpOnly=true, secure=https-scheme-only, sameSite=Lax, path=/) only used as a fallback when properties are unset — these mirror Spring Boot's WebSessionIdResolverAutoConfiguration. No logging in resolver or SecurityConfig (zero risk of session-id leakage from this commit). XSRF cookie flow (CookieServerCsrfTokenRepository + csrfCookieMaterializer in SecurityConfig.java:55-90) is on a different cookie name and untouched by the resolver swap. Missing/null/Boolean.FALSE REMEMBER_ME_ATTR collapses to a session-only cookie via builder-default Duration.ofSeconds(-1) (line 68-74) — the safe direction; never escalates to 30-day persistence; never bypasses authentication (the session id is still written, only Max-Age is omitted). Singleton bean has only final fields (serverProperties, rememberMeDays) plus the parent's once-set cookieName; setSessionId allocates a fresh ResponseCookieBuilder and PropertyMapper per call — no per-request mutation of bean state, race-free. Inherited resolveSessionIds and expireSession unchanged: pre-fix cookies (no Max-Age) still parse and resolve (Scenario G test confirms), and logout writes Max-Age=0 even when REMEMBER_ME_ATTR=Boolean.TRUE is present on the exchange (Scenario H test confirms). REMEMBER_ME_ATTR is written only from AuthService.openSession (single server-controlled write site driven by LoginRequest.rememberMe — already client-exposed via the login API) and read only by the resolver — no HTTP-header-to-attribute auto-binding in WebFlux, so external attribute injection is not possible. No hardcoded secrets in any of the changed files.
